I've got 20 mu here in Quzhou County, all in wheat-maize rotation. Ten years I've been at this, and I learned from my father and from watching which neighbors make money and which ones barely break even. I finished middle school, so I can read the fertilizer bags and calculate costs, but I don't trust outside advice unless I see it work in someone else's field first.

My winter wheat is Jimai 22, an improved variety. I switched to it five years ago when I saw Old Wang across the road get an extra 100 jin per mu with that seed while I was still using the old type. In October I do rotary tillage and sow. For fertilizer, I put down 100 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing time — that gives me about 6 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium per mu. Then I topdress urea twice: 50 jin per mu when the wheat greens up in spring, and another 30 jin at heading stage. All together that's about 15 kg nitrogen per mu. I irrigate four times through the season: winter water, jointing water, heading water, and grain filling water. My diesel pump from the well handles it fine. I spray pesticide twice — herbicide when the wheat is small, and a fungicide-insecticide mix when the weather warms up and the diseases start showing. If the weather is normal, I get about 550 kg per mu.

For summer maize, I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid seed. Everyone around here uses hybrid maize — the old open-pollinated types are a waste of good land. After wheat harvest in early June, I do quick rotary tillage and sow the same day. Summer season is short, you can't wait even two days. I put 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then 60 jin of urea at big-ear stage. That's about 16 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times: after sowing if the soil is dry, at jointing, and at filling stage. I spray twice: herbicide after the seedlings come up, and insecticide for corn borer when the plants are about waist-high. I expect 600 kg per mu.

Why these amounts? Because I've tested cutting back and it doesn't pay. Two years ago I skipped one urea topdressing on 5 mu to save about 200 yuan, and those 5 mu gave me 80 jin less per mu. At the price maize was that year, I lost over 500 yuan to save 200. That was stupid. Better to put a bit too much fertilizer than risk a bad harvest — losing crop is a disaster, but wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. I watch Zhang, who farms 18 mu down the road. He uses almost exactly what I use. If next year he changes something and his yield jumps, I'll copy him. That's how I decide.
